issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named _detect_errors(measurements, checks) (with a leading underscore), while the provided template and the reference solution use the name detect_errors(measurements, checks) (no leading underscore). This name mismatch between the problem description and the code can confuse students about which function to implement and may cause tests or instructions that reference _detect_errors to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to reference detect_errors(...) (no leading underscore), or rename the template/solution function to _detect_errors(...) and provide the corresponding alias or tests. Ensure all instructions and tests use the same identifier.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_detect_errors(...)`, but both the template and solution repositories define the function as `detect_errors(...)` (no leading underscore). This inconsistency between the task description and the provided code creates confusion about the expected identifier and may cause students to implement the wrong name or the autograder to fail to find the implemented function.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to request `detect_errors(measurements, checks)` (recommended), or (B) rename the function in the template and solution to `_detect_errors(...)` so it matches the problem text. Ensure tests and examples reference the same identifier.
